references: links and numbers only; drawings in git-ignored Data/Reference/raw/boats/J22/shape/
moves_ok_note: The deck, rails, cabin, cockpit and transom pieces are built on sheer_z/half_beam/deck_z, and the keel's root on keel_z, so a hull change moves them; each of those sections re-runs its checks (docs/shape-loop rule 4). This card changes the plan itself, so the deck hardware, rigging ends and interior placed from half_beam move with it ('other': chainplates and shrouds 4-8 cm inboard, stern cleats and backstay plates 31-34 cm, traveller ends 11 cm, keel bolts 7 mm down with the deeper canoe body); score.md lists every move for the review. The rudder and its fittings are not built on the hull curves and must not move.

plan.source: International J/22 Class Rules 2025, H.1 Plan E deck layout (j22.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/J22-Class-Rules-2025-1.pdf p.41). Traced as plan.mask.png, bow turned to the left; scaled so stem to transom = LOA 6.858 m, which gives beam 2.445 m (class 2.438), so the drawing is true to scale within 0.3%. Plan F (interior layout, same page) is stretched (L/B 2.89 against the class 2.81) and is not used.

profile.source: none yet: the class plans show only the stem and transom corners (Plan A). Commons has broadside photos out of the water (File:J-22 sailboat Jay2PLay on trailer.jpg, CC BY-SA 3.0; File:J22 sailboat on crane 8040.jpg) but upload.wikimedia.org refuses downloads from the cloud (HTTP 429); trace them on BEN-PC. Until then the profile is held by the ORC freeboards and the class LOA.

stern.source: none yet; the transom's width at the deck comes from Plan E (1.18 m)

findings: Baseline against Plan E: plan IoU 0.860; the deck line was up to 0.34 m a side too wide at the transom and 0.2 m at the forward quarter (rms 150 mm).

Round 1 kept the old body under the water and narrowed only the topsides: the bow sections had to turn upright just above the waterline (a crease). Bean chose (Nov 10) to narrow the underwater bow too and move the physics hull with it.

Round 5: the plan is a natural cubic spline fitted to the drawing (5 mm rms, no inflection); canoe depth 0.2072 m floats the physics' 1.052 m^3 (the old hero displaced 3.4% more than the physics: closed). CB moves 8 cm aft of the old physics hull's; the physics trims to it.
physics_note: Bean, Nov 10 (decision card): the underwater bow follows the drawing too, so the J/22's physics hull is now the hero's own sections (Tools/boats/j22/make_j22_hull.py writes SailingPhysics' J22HullData.inl), and the check holds the hero to the physics it ships with (BoatExport j22: 1.052 m^3, CB x -0.277 z -0.077) instead of to the old hero.
removes_ok_note: the traveller track is shorter across the narrower cockpit, so it has one screw fewer a side
